HOME AND DAILY LIFE LESSON · HOME AND DAILY LIFE · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Caring for Plants — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches the five things every plant needs — pot, soil, seed, water, sun — by planting one real seed that belongs entirely to the child.

What is this?

Caring for plants means giving them what they need: the pot to live in, the soil to root in, the seed to start from, the watering can to drink from, the sunlight to eat.

What does it mean?

A planted seed is a responsibility with a heartbeat — slow, forgiving, and entirely dependent on the child showing up. Miss a day, water twice; the plant forgives, and the habit forms.

What does the child need to know?

You need the card, one small pot, seed compost, one big seed (a bean or sunflower — both forgiving), a small watering can and the brightest windowsill in the house.

Why this matters

The crayon-line height chart is the lesson’s celebration: when the sprout appears, its height is marked and dated. Growing things get measured; pride gets recorded.

What it teaches

Sequencing a living process (pot, soil, seed, water, sun), daily care with real stakes, and patience — the slowest virtue, taught by the fastest forgiving teacher.

Words to learn

plant potseedsoilwatering cansunlightsprout

Say this to your child

“"Caring for plants! Soil in the pot, seed tucked in, one small drink, the sunniest window. Now the best part — every morning, we look. One day soon: a sprout, and it is YOURS."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "five things every plant needs — we have all five."
  2. Pot first: the child names it (their pot, their choice) and fills it with soil — hands in the dirt, that is the lesson signing on.
  3. The seed: one big seed, one finger-deep hole, tucked in with a pat.
  4. Water and sun: one small glug from the can — then the brightest sill, and the promise: we check every day.
  5. The waiting, done right: one check each morning, a small drink when the soil is dry — and when the sprout comes, the crayon line and the date.

Look closer at the picture

On this card the words "Caring for Plants" sit over a terracotta plant pot, one fat seed, a mound of dark soil, a blue watering can mid-pour and a bright sun with rays.

Ask your child

"What does the seed tuck into?" (the soil) "What does the plant drink?" (water from the can) "What does the plant eat?" (the sunlight)

What your child can say or do

Your child might check the pot before breakfast in pajamas, water it with tea-party precision, or draw the sprout taller than it is — with artistic license and total joy.

Out in the real world

Gardens, classrooms and community plots all run this sequence — pot, soil, seed, water, sun. A child who has raised one sprout is a gardener wherever a pot is offered.

Try it together

Sprout Height Chart: when the sprout appears, mark its height with a crayon line and the date — then mark again each week. The chart becomes the family’s slowest, proudest graph.

Understanding check

Ask: "What are the five things a plant needs?" (pot, soil, seed, water, sun) "How often do we check?" (every morning) "Whose sprout is it?" (say the name — the grower’s)

This lesson pairs with the Caring for Plants flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Home and Daily Life.
